walkthroughs.body_html:
Resource Reliance — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Resource Reliance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Resource Reliance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Africa
South America
Australia

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a four-figure and six-figure grid reference?
options: Six-figure references are just longer versions of the same thing.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Four-figure references identify a 1km square (eastings then northings); six-figure references pinpoint a location within that square to 100m accuracy by adding tenths.
Four-figure references are for OS maps and six-figure references are for atlases.
